ideas.title: Entitlement drift tester
ideas.summary: AI-native SaaS teams are adding usage billing, plan gates, and agent-built features faster than their entitlement logic can be trusted. A solo builder could ship a lightweight verifier that replays Stripe events, checks feature-flag state, and runs GUI/API probes as each plan tier to catch users who paid for X but can access Y before support or revenue leakage finds it.

evidence.note: SaaS founder asks how to manage plan entitlements and detect drift between purchased and actual access.
Ask HN asks how to handle billing when event volume exceeds Stripe limits, a related usage-billing correctness pain.
VISTA suggests more robust GUI grounding checks, useful for synthetic users verifying plan-gated screens.
AI SDK harness and sandbox support gives a practical execution layer for repeatable entitlement probes.

ideas.title: Agent skill governance
ideas.summary: Agent skills are turning into installable third-party workflows, but teams lack the package-review layer they already expect for dependencies. A solo builder could ship a skill registry proxy that scans skill packs, records provenance, checks tool permissions, enforces team policy, and produces a short risk report before a skill is imported into Claude, Codex, or internal agent runners.

evidence.note: SkillSpector trended as a scanner for vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, and security risks in AI agent skills.
ToolSense proposes auditing tool knowledge against a catalog, pointing to governance needs around agent tool and skill interfaces.
Airtable's public Hyperagent skill pack adds a credible third-party supply signal that teams may want to inspect before adoption.

ideas.title: Agent flow manager
ideas.summary: AI coding broke the old deep-work rhythm: slow agents create idle gaps, too many parallel tasks create context debt, and overnight delegation still needs human checkpoints. A solo builder could ship a local workroom for Codex and Claude that batches tasks, runs agents on a cadence, suppresses low-value notifications, shows only blocked decisions, and produces a morning handoff so builders stay in flow while agents keep moving.

evidence.note: Claude Code sub-agents can spawn sub-agents, making parallel async work easier and increasing the need for attention management.
Ask HN: developers say agentic coding is disrupting flow state because slow agents interrupt the old rhythm of deep work.
Anthropic Labs workflow advice emphasizes overnight delegation and verification, which needs a better human handoff surface.
Agentsview trended as local-first session intelligence across coding agents, supporting a control-room surface for async agent work.
The flow-state thread recurred in today's demand signals, keeping attention fragmentation from slow coding agents as an active pain.
Conan launched as a native Mac cockpit for Claude Code, validating demand for an operator surface around coding agents.
Loop-engineering thread formalizes the scheduler, maker, checker, and escalation structure behind long-running agent work.

ideas.title: Agent spend guard
ideas.summary: Fable-class agents are creating a new operations problem: builders can burn subscription quota or API dollars before they know which task, loop, or stack decision caused it. Solo builders and small teams would pay for a local proxy and dashboard that meters every agent run, flags runaway loops, compares implementation paths by token burn, and routes mechanical work to cheaper models before the quota wall hits.

evidence.note: Tell HN: a $200-plan subscriber burned most of a weekly quota in one day on Fable 5 — acute, unmet cost-visibility pain.
Easybilling launched AI-native billing for usage-based AI products — the payments side is taken, the spend-control side is open.
Agentsview trended as local-first session intelligence for coding agents, showing momentum around usage analytics rather than billing alone.
Tell HN: a $200-plan subscriber says one day of Fable work consumed 45% of weekly quota, keeping cost visibility as an active pain point.
A builder reports cutting a Fable build from 5.5M to 2.3M tokens by changing the implementation path, proving workflow design changes cost materially.
OpenAI rolled out bankable Codex rate-limit resets — quota scarcity is now visible enough to become a product mechanic.
Bookmarked Rilable launch says a 10-prompt Fable 5 build cost roughly $210 on API pricing, reinforcing the need for task-level spend controls.
shadcn/improve again supports a high-model-plans, cheap-model-executes pattern that a spend guard could recommend automatically.
The Fable expense thread recurred, reinforcing quota burn and task-level cost visibility as unresolved builder pain.
SaaS founder asks for agent revenue, compute cost, gross profit, and human intervention data in one view.
Builder thread says Claude Max can burn through a $200 subscription quickly when Fable-class workflows are misrouted.
OpenRouter Fusion positions model fusion as a cheaper path to near-frontier quality, reinforcing routing as spend control.

ideas.title: Bring-your-own-agent code review
ideas.summary: Review is becoming an orchestration workflow, not a single SaaS endpoint: teams want repo-aware checks, per-file specialists, and merge stewardship without paying a metered review vendor for work their own Claude, Codex, or Copilot subscription can do. The wedge is a bring-your-own-agent reviewer that runs locally or in CI, fans out review tasks, preserves a checklist per repo, and hands humans only the decisions that matter.

evidence.note: Claude Code v2.1.172 lets sub-agents spawn sub-agents up to 5 levels deep — the capability that makes per-file review fan-out trivial.
Ask HN: paying CodeRabbit customer hit a 2-reviews-per-hour throttle and is actively looking for alternatives.
SkillSpector validates the need for security checks around imported agent skills and review workflows.
shadcn/improve packages frontier-model repo audits into plans that cheaper models can execute, matching the review-planning half of the idea.
Patchrooms launched around turning app feedback into agent-ready patch context, adjacent to bring-your-own-agent repair.
A widely shared autonomous repo loop frames triage, autoreview, and merge work as an agent team that can wake on a schedule.
GitHub promoted a Copilot app for finding work, implementing, and stewarding PRs through merge, validating demand while staying inside the Copilot ecosystem.
TestSprite CLI trended as AI-powered testing from the terminal, adjacent to automated review verification before merge.
Ask HN: builders want a metric for AI code quality, strengthening the case for repo-aware review and verification workflows.
SkillSpector continued trending, validating security checks around imported agent skills and review workflows.
Agent Beacon promotes normalized, enterprise-owned execution traces for endpoint, CI, and cloud agents.
Vercel AI SDK canary adds harness support for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi, making bring-your-own-agent review sessions easier to run.
